title: Choose Lectern's visual world
question: Choose the system that should make focused reading and annotation feel unmistakably clear.

options.label: The Transparent Desk
options.lineage: architectural tracing overlays and registration drafting
options.thesis: The PDF is the drawing; notes live on a visible, reversible working layer.
options.viewport: A full-height paper canvas commands the center while a slim navigation rail and contextual instrument tray frame it without stealing focus.
options.risk: Too many drafting cues could make a calm reader feel like specialist CAD software.

raised.raise: Active tools receive instrument-grade status feedback and a concise live readout.
Unfamiliar controls keep direct labels until their meaning becomes obvious.
Selected color and width states move decisively forward instead of changing by a few pixels.

options.label: The Scholar's Margin
options.lineage: annotated monographs, proofreader marks, and working marginalia
options.thesis: A calm reading desk where annotation tools behave like a precise modern margin.
options.viewport: The document owns most of the window; a quiet top bar handles navigation and an expandable margin holds note tools and history.
options.risk: This is the most familiar direction and can feel conservative unless the margin interaction is exceptionally crafted.

options.label: Reading Itinerary
options.lineage: segmented boarding passes and live gate boards
options.thesis: Every page is a leg in a reading journey, with progress and annotation changes held visibly in place.
options.viewport: A precise status strip ranks document, page, zoom, and save state while the PDF and detachable annotation segment sit below.
options.case: It matches product clarity through exceptional state signaling, but focused readers identify less strongly with travel infrastructure.
options.risk: The journey metaphor may become louder than the long-form reading task.

options.label: Signal Bench
options.lineage: CRT oscilloscopes and calibrated signal benches
options.thesis: Reading and ink become channels on one precision instrument.
options.viewport: The PDF sits inside an instrument bezel with tool controls arranged as calibrated channels.
options.case: The active-state model is excellent, but the scientific hardware identity overwhelms books and sustained reading.
options.risk: Long sessions would feel visually intense and genre-specific.

options.label: Data Field
options.thesis: Pages and marks become a strict field of indexed information.
options.viewport: A black-and-white page field is indexed by dense page and mark coordinates.
options.case: The system is rigorous, but it sacrifices reading comfort and gives annotation color no honest role.
options.risk: High visual tension works against prolonged reading.

options.label: Labeled Cutaway
options.thesis: Every reading control explains itself directly in one continuous labeled scene.
options.viewport: The reader opens as a labeled cutaway where each tool reveals its purpose beside the page.
options.case: Its discoverability is strong, but the illustrative world conflicts with focused academic reading.
options.risk: The interface risks feeling instructional after the first session.

options.label: Box Archive
options.lineage: stacked sneaker boxes and indexed end labels
options.thesis: Documents and tools are selected by pulling a clearly labeled object from an archive wall.
options.viewport: The PDF slides from a document stack while the active tool projects from a labeled tray.
options.case: Selection states are tangible, but the archive metaphor serves a library screen better than the reader itself.
options.kept: Decisive selected states that visibly move forward.
options.risk: Object theater would consume space needed by the document.

options.label: Balanced Forces
options.thesis: Reading, navigation, and annotation are exposed as one balanced system.
options.viewport: The document is held by a visible network linking page state to contextual controls.
options.case: The relationships are clear in theory, but the spatial metaphor makes ordinary PDF actions unfamiliar.
options.kept: Every contextual option remains visibly connected to its active tool.
options.risk: Novel navigation would slow experienced readers.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A familiar desktop PDF reader executed with excellent hierarchy and interaction polish.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional top toolbar, centered document, and persistent right annotation sidebar.
canonCard.risk: It is immediately usable but intentionally indistinguishable from established PDF readers.
